title: Hidden in the Shadows
summary: The web admin swears the web server has no secrets. But not every file shows up at first glance.
briefing:
Thanks to your report, DotTech changed the admin password. Now they want you to check their web server, dottech-web.

The website's files live in `/var/www`. The web admin promises that nothing secret is stored there: "I checked it myself – it's clean!"

On Linux, though, some files are hidden. Prove the admin wrong.
objective: Find the secret file hidden in /var/www and read the flag inside it.
debrief:
Nice work! On Linux, any file whose name starts with a dot – like `.secret_flag` – is hidden from a normal `ls`.

With `ls -a` (or `ls -la` for details) you can see everything. Hidden files are not a security feature: they just keep folders tidy. Attackers always look for them.

The lesson for DotTech: if a file is secret, protect it with permissions – or don't put it on a web server at all.
hints: On Linux, files whose names start with a dot (`.`) are hidden. They don't show up when you just type `ls`.
Go to the folder with `cd /var/www`, then list everything – hidden files too – with `ls -a` or `ls -la`. In the Files app, turn on "Show hidden files".
